correctness.rationale: The exact matrix element is a polar radial incomplete-gamma integral. At a disk the vacuum e_0 is the simple maximal eigenvector with lambda_0-lambda_n=e^{-s}A_n(s)>=s e^{-s}; the bounded compactly supported coherent-projector integral is twice trace-norm differentiable for each fixed s,h. Standard isolated-eigenvalue second-order perturbation yields vacuum curvature -e^{-s}||h||^2/2 plus the positive resolvent correction e^{-s}a_n/A_n for each Fourier amplitude; Parseval gives the asserted d_n. The falling-factorial reciprocal sum A_n/a_n strictly increases in n, and a Poisson-probability ratio plus ordinary and local CLT give the large-s crossover. Independently constructed truncated Fock concentration matrices from angular quadrature reproduce five even-in-epsilon curvatures and a Poisson-edge ratio. No uniform nonlinear remainder in s or n is asserted.

value.rationale: A natural sharp stability question for the maximizer of the Gaussian time-frequency Faber–Krahn problem: identifies precisely the translation nullspace, least stable nontrivial angular frequency, sharp area-dependent curvature, and normal-hazard spectral transition. These provide an exact structural Hessian rather than merely a qualitative global inequality.

final_claim: For each fixed s>0 and real C^2 zero-mean boundary mode h with r^2<s+epsilon h(theta), the optimized Fock top eigenvalue has epsilon^2 coefficient -e^{-s} sum_{n>=2}(1-a_n/A_n)|hhat_n|^2, a_n=s^n/n!, A_n=sum_{j=1}^n s^j/j!. The coefficients increase strictly with d_1=0 and d_2=2/(s+2), giving the sharp transverse L2 coefficient e^{-s}/(s+2). If n/s tends alpha>=0, d_n tends min(alpha,1), and at n=s+u sqrt(s)+o(sqrt(s)), sqrt(s)(1-d_n) tends phi(u)/Phi(u).
limitations: Fixed positive area and fixed real mean-zero C2 h; epsilon->0 first; no uniform perturbation remainder in area or mode.
The theorem is an optimized spectral local statement, not a global sharp nonlinear stability bound.
